cues.text: Hi there, welcome to the Job Centre. How can I help?
cues.speaker: Manager

cues.text: Good morning, I’m here to enquire as to whether you have any jobs available at the moment?
cues.speaker: Lauren

cues.text: Yes, we have several available. What kind of job is it that you’re looking for?
cues.speaker: Manager

cues.text: Well, um, I’ll take any Example part-time jobs I can get.
cues.speaker: Lauren

cues.text: I’m really strapped for cash at the moment.
cues.speaker: Lauren

cues.text: Okay, bear with me while I have a browse on our system.
cues.speaker: Manager

cues.text: Here  we are. We have three vacancies at the moment, all involving quite different roles.
cues.speaker: Manager

cues.text: That sounds promising. What are they?
cues.speaker: Lauren

cues.text: The ﬁrst one is for a post as a receptionist.
cues.speaker: Manager

cues.text: It says here that experience in reception or general administration is preferred, but not essential.
cues.speaker: Manager

cues.text: Have you worked on a reception desk previously?
cues.speaker: Manager

cues.text: No, I haven’t. I had a baby quite young, and so I have very little work experience.
cues.speaker: Lauren

cues.text: Could you tell me a few more details?
cues.speaker: Lauren

cues.text: Yes, of course. The job will be to mainly provide quality customer service both over the phone and in person.
cues.speaker: Manager

cues.text: When customers are waiting you will be expected to provide them with refreshments and ensure they have a ﬁrst-rate experience.
cues.speaker: Manager

cues.text: I think I could manage that, and I’m a very friendly person!
cues.speaker: Lauren

cues.text: That’s great.
cues.speaker: Manager

cues.text: Do you have any information about the hours involved?
cues.speaker: Lauren

cues.text: It says here that you will be expected to work several early mornings, 4 days a week.
cues.speaker: Manager

cues.text: Any other requirements?
cues.speaker: Lauren

cues.text: Yeah, you’ll have to go through a couple of weeks of unpaid training before qualifying for the post.
cues.speaker: Manager

cues.text: Hmm, I don’t know if I would be able to fully commit to that. Did you say it’s 4 days per week?
cues.speaker: Lauren

cues.text: Yeah, it says here 4 days a week, with another day oﬀ per week when requested in advance.
cues.speaker: Manager

cues.text: It also explicitly states that at least one of your working days must fall on a weekend.
cues.speaker: Manager

cues.text: I’ll have to think about that and talk to my babysitter.
cues.speaker: Lauren

cues.text: Are there any other roles beginning later in the day?
cues.speaker: Lauren

cues.text: Yes, there’s an advertisement here for a driver.
cues.speaker: Manager

cues.text: It says you’ll need a clean and valid UK driver’s license, with absolutely no exception.
cues.speaker: Manager

cues.text: No problems there. I passed my test ﬁrst time and have never received any points.
cues.speaker: Lauren

cues.text: It also explicitly states that you must be over twenty-ﬁve and have been driving for at least six years.
cues.speaker: Manager

cues.text: That sounds quite exciting. Is there any more information?
cues.speaker: Lauren

cues.text: Yep, it says here that working hours are flexible, and the employers are happy to work within your personal schedule since they employ multiple drivers.
cues.speaker: Manager

cues.text: That’s great.
cues.speaker: Lauren

cues.text: The employers ask for a commitment to either mornings 5 days per week, evenings 5 days per week, or three full working days per week.
cues.speaker: Manager

cues.text: I’m sure I can handle all that without a problem.
cues.speaker: Lauren

cues.text: As well as driving the employers to and from work, they will ask you to perform various duties on their behalf, such as collecting the grocery shopping, and picking their children up from school.
cues.speaker: Manager

cues.text: Do they need me to work a day on the weekend as well?
cues.speaker: Lauren

cues.text: No, it says here that they only require you to work on weekdays, not weekends.
cues.speaker: Manager

cues.text: That sounds interesting.
cues.speaker: Lauren

cues.text: Okay, there’s only one more left, another customer service-related post.
cues.speaker: Manager

cues.text: It looks like it requires you to work short hours, quite late at night, so it might not be suitable for you.
cues.speaker: Manager

cues.text: Do you want to hear about it anyway?
cues.speaker: Manager

cues.text: Yeah, can’t do any harm.
cues.speaker: Lauren

cues.text: Okay, so it’s a post for a cashier in acinema in the centre of town.
cues.speaker: Manager

cues.text: I’m sure you’ve been to the cinema a few times, so you can guess what kind of role it would be.
cues.speaker: Manager

cues.text: They’re quite short and late shifts, between 17.30 and 22.30 most nights, with slightly longer shifts on Friday and Saturday nights.
cues.speaker: Manager

cues.text: Mmm, can you tell me what the job involves?
cues.speaker: Lauren

cues.text: Yes, sure. It says that you’ll be required to sell and dispense tickets, and provide refreshments.
cues.speaker: Manager

cues.text: Also, they ask that you be quick on the computers since you’ll also need to take bookings over the phone, but you’ll receive basic training for that.
cues.speaker: Manager

cues.text: Do they need me to work weekdays as well?
cues.speaker: Lauren

cues.text: Well, it says here that if you request at least a fortnight in advance, they will grant you a day off on Mondays, but never on a weekend.
cues.speaker: Manager

cues.text: Mmm. I’ll think it over and let you know later. Thanks for all your help.
cues.speaker: Lauren
